<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only executes the top-level code in the PKGBUILD file itself. It does not run the `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions, nor does it execute any commands from the `source` array or other scoped functions. The file contains only standard variable definitions (e.g., `pkgver`, `_pkgver`, `_subver`, `_commit`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, etc.) and a `source=` array that merely declares where the source code comes from — it does not actually clone or execute any remote content during this step. There are no command substitutions, shell invocations, or network operations in the global scope that could execute untrusted payloads. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are defined but remain uninvoked by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so they cannot execute malicious code at this stage. Therefore, this command is safe to run.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No dangerous code in top-level scope; only variable definitions and source declaration.</summary>
